Package neqsim.process.operations.replay

Class ReplayResult

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.operations.replay.ReplayResult
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class ReplayResult extends Object implements Serializable
Result of a ProcessReplay: per-step records, residual statistics, baseline standardisation and change-point detection, with CSV and JSON export.

Residual statistics only use converged steps with a finite residual. Windows are given as inclusive start and exclusive end row indices; rowIndexAtOrAfter(double) converts a time stamp to an index.

Version:
1.0
Author:
ESOL

    • detectChangePoints

      public List<ReplayResult.ChangePoint> detectChangePoints(String tag, double slack, double threshold, double minSigma)
      Detects shifts in the residual of a tag with a two-sided tabular CUSUM on the standardised residuals.

      With z the standardised residual, S+ = max(0, S+ + z - k) and S- = max(0, S- - z - k). A change is confirmed when either sum exceeds h; the change time is the maximum-likelihood mean-shift split between the row after the sum was last zero and the confirmation row. The sums are then reset and the reference level is moved to the mean standardised residual over at least 10 rows from the change (the analysis is offline, so later rows may be used), so a sustained shift is reported once and later shifts are measured from the new level. Rows without a residual are skipped.

      Parameters:
      tag - measured output tag
      slack - reference value k in standard deviations (typically 0.5)
      threshold - decision interval h in standard deviations (typically 4 to 5)
      minSigma - lower bound on the baseline standard deviation
      Returns:
      detected change points in time order
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if no baseline window is set

    • refineChangeIndex

      private static int refineChangeIndex(double[] z, int first, int end, double level)
      Refines a CUSUM change-time estimate with the maximum-likelihood split for a mean shift: among candidate start rows between the last zero of the CUSUM and the detection row, select the row maximising n * (mean(z[t..end]) - level)^2.
      Parameters:
      z - standardised residuals (NaN for missing rows)
      first - first candidate row (first row after the CUSUM was last zero)
      end - detection row (inclusive)
      level - reference level before the change
      Returns:
      estimated row where the shift started
